description: United States: the Statutes at Large (read on the Library of Congress page images) and newspapers of November 1883 read on Chronicling America page images (Library of Congress) on the retrieval date.

citations.title: An Act To save daylight and to provide standard time for the United States (ch. 24, approved March 19, 1918), section 1
citations.issuer: Congress of the United States (65th Congress)
citations.publication: United States Statutes at Large, vol. 40, pp. 450-451
citations.excerpt: The standard time of the first zone shall be based on the mean astronomical time of the seventy-fifth degree of longitude west from Greenwich; that of the second zone on the ninetieth degree

citations.title: An Act To save daylight and to provide standard time for the United States (ch. 24, approved March 19, 1918), section 3
citations.issuer: Congress of the United States (65th Congress)
citations.publication: United States Statutes at Large, vol. 40, p. 451
citations.excerpt: at two o'clock antemeridian of the last Sunday in March of each year the standard time of each zone shall be advanced one hour, and at two o'clock antemeridian of the last Sunday in October [...] by the retarding of one hour, be returned

citations.title: An Act For the repeal of the daylight-saving law (ch. 51, August 20, 1919; passed over the President's veto)
citations.issuer: Congress of the United States (66th Congress)
citations.publication: United States Statutes at Large, vol. 41, p. 280
citations.excerpt: That section 3 of the Act entitled "An Act to save daylight and to provide standard time for the United States," approved March 19, 1918, is hereby repealed, effective on the last Sunday of October, 1919

citations.title: An act to establish a standard of time in the District of Columbia (ch. 12, approved March 13, 1884)
citations.issuer: Congress of the United States (48th Congress)
citations.publication: United States Statutes at Large, vol. 23, p. 4
citations.excerpt: That the legal standard of time in the District of Columbia shall hereafter be the mean time of the seventy-fifth meridian of longitude west from Greenwich.

citations.title: Standard Time in New York
citations.excerpt: The mayor has signed the resolution changing the city time and reading "that at noon, November 18, 1883, and thereafter all time in the city of New York shall conform to the new standard [...] and that all time shown by the public clocks shall agree therewith."

citations.title: New York Time at an End: the Old Standard Dropped, and the New One Adopted
citations.excerpt: lifting a pin, stopped the great clock at 12 minutes past 12 o'clock. Three minutes 58 seconds and 38-100 seconds later he started the works again. Thus the metropolis officially recognized the new time
citations.gloss: The City Hall clock was stopped for 3 min 58.38 s to bring it from New York time to Eastern standard time.

citations.title: Standard Time in Baltimore
citations.excerpt: The new time standard of the 75th meridian, which advances Baltimore time six minutes and twenty-eight seconds, goes into effect here at noon to-morrow. [...] and city time reckoned by it.

citations.title: How Father Time Was Robbed of Eight Minutes Yesterday
citations.excerpt: The business men generally who have no connection with the railroads will keep the old time, regulating their watches by the bells at noon. [...] The clocks in the up-town departments have not been changed to correspond with the new time

citations.title: How Father Time Was Robbed of Eight Minutes Yesterday: the fire bells to give both times
citations.excerpt: the naval observatory will signal every day the new time, eight minutes and twelve seconds earlier, when the fire-alarm bells will each strike one simultaneously; then, eight minutes and twelve seconds later, they will strike the usual number (twelve) on the same bells.
citations.gloss: Washington noon came 8 min 12 s after Eastern standard noon.

citations.title: Local news (the railroads centering in Providence adopt standard time)
citations.excerpt: which will be a set back of 14 minutes and 40 seconds, thus the railroad time will be fifteen minutes slower than Providence time.

citations.title: Local news (the new standard of time in Pawtucket and Providence)
citations.excerpt: The Providence authorities, as in other important matters, procrastinated, and did not "come to (the new) time" until Tuesday.
citations.gloss: Providence adopted standard time on Tuesday 20 November 1883.

citations.title: The Change in Time: the Standard Time Duly Adopted
citations.excerpt: The new change in time, the central standard, as it is called, went into effect at 12 o'clock, noon, yesterday, and the jewelers of the city will to-day change their regulators to correspond.

citations.title: The Change in Time: the Standard Time Duly Adopted
citations.excerpt: Yesterday afternoon the court-house clock was set back sixteen minutes, and is now speeding along, judging from its placid face, wholly oblivious of the change.

citations.title: Local notes (standard time in Louisville)
citations.excerpt: Dr. E. A. Grant, of Louisville, is the father of the "standard time" arrangement [...] In that city the fire bells rang at twelve o'clock, new time, and the city clock was turned back 18 minutes.

citations.title: By Meridian Ninety: the New Standard Time Went into Effect at Noon Yesterday
citations.issuer: The Rock Island Argus (Rock Island, Ill.)
citations.excerpt: The central time is based upon that of the 90th meridian, which is nine minutes slower than Chicago time.

citations.title: Standard Time
citations.excerpt: The Chicago papers of Sunday, give full accounts, illustrated by maps, of the change in the standard time inaugurated in that city on Sunday noon. The new time standard has been adopted [...] by the Board of Trade and a number of hotels

citations.title: New Standard Time: Its Adoption To-Day Throughout the Whole Northwest
citations.publication: The St. Paul Sunday Globe, 25 November 1883
citations.excerpt: At noon to-day in St. Paul and throughout this part of the northwest the new standard time will be inaugurated.

citations.title: New Standard Time: Its Adoption To-Day Throughout the Whole Northwest
citations.publication: The St. Paul Sunday Globe, 25 November 1883
citations.excerpt: Our new time will be twelve minutes faster than the old time, which places us only three degrees east of our former meantime.

citations.title: New Standard Time: Its Adoption To-Day Throughout the Whole Northwest
citations.publication: The St. Paul Sunday Globe, 25 November 1883
citations.excerpt: The city council and chamber of commerce have adopted it.

citations.title: Minneapolis Globules
citations.publication: The St. Paul Sunday Globe, 25 November 1883
citations.excerpt: The new standard time will be generally adopted in Minneapolis to-day.
